scenario_prompt: Write the risk section of a solution proposal, naming each material risk and what is done about it, and stating plainly any risk that cannot be fully retired rather than omitting it. Context: the buyer's RFP requires a SOC 2 Type II report and the bidder holds only a SOC 2 Type I report today, with the Type II observation window closing after the RFP's submission date; separately, the bidder's own most comparable prior migration took 11 months, close to the buyer's 6-month compliance-audit deadline. Return only the risk section text.
text:
**Artifact family: a proposal section.**

Customer source material for this section means the RFP question text, the buyer's stated compliance-audit deadline and its consequences, discovery notes, and any prior-engagement records you hold. None was supplied for this task, so the `PF-3.3` provenance override cannot fire and every term below is judged by the deletion test alone. Supply that material and I will re-run against the buyer's own vocabulary.

---

## Risks

You are running a migration against a fixed compliance-audit deadline six months out, and you are asking a bidder to carry attestation evidence you can hand to your auditor. Two risks in this bid are material, and one of them cannot be fully retired before you sign. We state both plainly here rather than in a schedule you would have to find.

**Risk 1 — We hold a SOC 2 Type I report today, not the Type II report your RFP requires.**

Our current attestation is SOC 2 Type I [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): confirm report date, auditing firm, and scope against the RFP's stated control requirements before submission]. A Type I report attests control design at a point in time. Your RFP requires Type II, which attests operating effectiveness across an observation window. Our Type II observation window closes after your submission date [PF-2.11 GAP: window close date and expected report issue date were not supplied — both are needed here]. We therefore cannot present a Type II report at bid evaluation.

This risk cannot be fully retired before you award. We do not propose to describe it as low. What we will do about it: we will provide the Type I report and the auditor's control matrix at submission, so you can assess design coverage now. We will issue the Type II report to you as soon as our auditor releases it [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): this is a date-shaped undertaking dependent on a third-party auditor — confirm it is deliverable and confirm the contractual form before this ships]. We will accept a contract term making Type II delivery a condition of continued engagement, at your discretion. The residual risk you carry is the gap between award and report issue. If your audit requires Type II evidence inside that gap, this bid does not meet that requirement and you should weigh it accordingly.

**Risk 2 — Our most comparable prior migration took 11 months against your 6-month deadline.**

The closest comparable engagement we can produce ran 11 months end to end [PF-2.15 REVIEW (reference): confirm disclosure permission before naming the client or describing their estate]. That is five months longer than the window you have. We are not presenting that duration as a worst case that will not recur. It is our own record, and it is the honest basis for planning.

We have not yet established which parts of that 11 months are attributable to scope, to environment, or to client-side dependencies [PF-2.11 GAP: the phase-level duration breakdown from the prior engagement was not supplied — without it we cannot state how much of the overrun is addressable]. Until that breakdown exists, no schedule commitment from us is evidenced.

What we will do about it: we will deliver the phase-level breakdown of the 11-month engagement within the clarification period, so you can judge transferability yourself rather than take our summary. We will propose a phased cutover that reaches audit-relevant scope first, so your compliance deadline is served even if full migration runs past it. We will agree a mid-point schedule checkpoint with a stated decision right for you if the plan is behind.

The residual risk you carry is schedule. On our own evidence, full migration inside six months is not something we have done before.

**Risk 3 — Comparative position.**

[PF-2.13 GAP: no differentiator is stated in this section, because no evidenced statement of what we do that bears on these two risks was supplied. A claim here without evidence would be the kind of assertion this section exists to avoid.]

---

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| `REVIEW (compliance)` on the SOC 2 Type I statement | PF-2.17 | Report date, auditing firm, and scope, checked against the RFP's stated control requirements |
| `GAP` on the Type II observation window | PF-2.11 | The window's close date and the auditor's expected report issue date |
| `REVIEW (commitment)` on Type II delivery | PF-2.14 | Confirmation the undertaking is deliverable, and the contractual form it should take |
| `REVIEW (reference)` on the prior migration | PF-2.15 | Client disclosure permission before naming them or describing their estate |
| `GAP` on the 11-month breakdown | PF-2.11 | Phase-level durations from the prior engagement, to show what is addressable |
| `GAP` on differentiators | PF-2.13 | An evidenced statement of vendor capability bearing on either risk |
